🇰🇪 DIPLOMATIC NUMBER PLATE CODES IN KENYA — EXPLAINED

Have you ever spotted a red number plate with “CD” or “UN” on Kenyan roads and wondered what it means?

Kenya issues distinctive red number plates to diplomatic missions and international organisations accredited to the country. These plates are not random — they carry specific codes that identify the country or organisation represented.

🔍 HOW TO READ A DIPLOMATIC PLATE

Example: 77 CD 1K

 • 77 → Country or organisation code
 • CD → Corps Diplomatique (Diplomatic Mission)
 • 1 → Rank/sequence of the vehicle (often the Ambassador’s car)
 • K → Vehicle registered in Kenya

The country codes were assigned in the order in which countries recognized Kenya’s independence or established diplomatic relations.

These identifiers help:
 • Law enforcement agencies
 • NTSA
 • Other government departments
to easily identify and regulate diplomatic vehicles.

To improve service delivery, the Government of Kenya established the GoK–UN Service Centre in Gigiri, allowing diplomats to access NTSA and other government services under one roof.

🇦🇺 MUSLIM HERO WHO STOPPED SYDNEY MASSACRE GETS HOSPITAL VISIT FROM RABBI'S FAMILY

Sunday night, Bondi Beach. 2 gunmen open fire on a Hanukkah celebration. 15 dead, including Rabbi Eli Schlanger who organized the event. 

Holocaust survivor Alex Kleytman murdered shielding his wife. A 10-year-old girl died, too.

Ahmed Al-Ahmad, 43-year-old Syrian-Australian fruit seller, watched from behind a parked car. 

Told his cousin "I'm going to die" - then charged the shooter anyway.

Wrestled away a rifle. Got shot 5 times by the second gunman. 1 bullet still lodged in his shoulder. 

Might lose his arm. Said he'd do it again.

Fast forward to his hospital bed: The brother-in-law of murdered Rabbi Schlanger visits Ahmed. 

"Thank you for your courage. The fact that you come from a Muslim background rather than a Jewish one is special."

Ahmed's response: 

"No matter what happens, we are all human beings, and no matter what religion, we must be together and save lives."

His father, who fled Syria and just reunited with him in Australia this year, said Ahmed's "conscience and soul" made him act.

Bill Ackman donated $99,999 - the GoFundMe max. Total raised: over $1.65 million. 

Prime Minister visited him. Trump called him "very, very brave." Israeli PM Netanyahu praised him.

Muslim leaders in Sydney went further - they're refusing to accept the body of the terrorist or conduct Islamic burial rites. Complete rejection.

This is the story they want buried under headlines about "rising tensions" and "interfaith dialogue programs." 

One Syrian refugee with 5 bullets in him just did more for Jewish-Muslim relations than a thousand nonprofit conferences.

The attackers? Father-son duo who traveled to the Philippines last month for "military-style training" with suspected ISIS links. Father killed at scene, son hospitalized facing charges.

Australia's worst mass shooting in decades just proved that courage doesn't check religion at the door. 

And the people writing checks for Ahmed's recovery aren't doing interfaith theater - they're honoring someone who bled for them.

Sometimes humanity wins. This was one of those times.

Sources: Chabad .org, CBS News, Al Jazeera, ABC News, Times of Israel, @JewishWarrior13
